title: Cartesian quasi-coherent module families on localized etale charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X/S$ an algebraic space with its small etale ringed site [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A cartesian module chart family consists of a module sheaf $F_V$ on the localized ringed site $X_{\mathrm{et}}/V$ for every $V\in X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and an isomorphism $c_f:f^*F_V\to F_W$ for every $f:W\to V$, where $f^*$ is the existing restriction along the functor $\mathcal C/W\to\mathcal C/V$. Require $c_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $c_{fg}=c_g\circ g^*c_f$ after the canonical identity and composition reindexings. A morphism $h:F\to G$ consists of module maps $h_V:F_V\to G_V$ satisfying $h_Wc_f^F=c_f^Gf^*h_V$ for every $f$. Identities and composition are componentwise. The category of cartesian quasi-coherent chart families is the full subcategory where each $F_V$ is quasi-coherent in the local-presentation sense [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. The iterated-slice sheafification and locally-bijective-equivalence instances used by this predicate are transported from $X_{\mathrm{et}}/W$ along the canonical equivalence $(X_{\mathrm{et}}/V)/(W\to V)\simeq X_{\mathrm{et}}/W$.
